mainTopic: The powers of לגימה, why some wicked kings are left out of the משנה, חזקיהו and the Babylonian messengers, and the opening פסוק of איכה
overview: This amud finishes רבי יוחנן's list of the five powers of לגימה, the food given to guests. Each power has a source: עמון and מואב, יתרו, מיכה, the colleague of עדו הנביא, and יהונתן failing to give דוד bread. The גמרא then asks why the משנה leaves the wicked kings אחז, אמון and יהויקים off the list of those with no share in עולם הבא. It teaches that a righteous son brings merit to his father, but a father cannot save his son. It also tells the story of יהויקים's skull, which was burned. Next comes a ברייתא showing how חזקיהו's self-praise led to non-Jews eating at his table and to the exile of his children. The גמרא then gives three views of what חזקיהו showed the Babylonian messengers. Finally, it explains the opening פסוק of איכה phrase by phrase. The amud ends as a story about two captives on הר הכרמל begins, and the story continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Hospitality pushes away the near: the source is עמון and מואב
steps.stepSummary: The first power of לגימה, that it 'distances the near,' is proven from עמון and מואב.
steps.simpleTranslation: (It distances the near) — we learn this from עמון and מואב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its first example. The rule that refusing food can push away even relatives comes from עמון and מואב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עמון and מואב were relatives of the Jewish people, since they come from לוט. They failed to greet the Jews with bread and water in the desert, and so their converts may never marry into the Jewish people. Holding back food turned close relatives into permanent outsiders.

keyTerms.meaning: A mouthful or sip; here it means food and drink given to guests
Two nations descended from לוט, nephew of אברהם
It distances the near (the first power, stated just before this section)

steps.confusionAlert: This line is the end of a sentence that started earlier: 'It distances the near.' Only the source, 'from עמון and מואב,' appears here.

phrases.english: From Ammon and Moab.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵעַמּוֹן וּמוֹאָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the first item of רבי יוחנן's list, which began before this section.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The case of עמון and מואב, relatives who were permanently excluded for not offering bread and water.

steps.title: Hospitality brings close the distant: the source is יתרו
steps.stepSummary: The second power, that לגימה 'draws near the distant,' is proven from יתרו. Because he invited משה to eat, his descendants sat in the לשכת הגזית.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it draws near the distant: we learn this from יתרו. As רבי יוחנן says: as a reward for saying 'Call him, that he may eat bread,' יתרו's grandchildren merited to sit in the לשכת הגזית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second example. יתרו, an outsider, invited משה for a meal, and as a reward his descendants reached the highest place of Torah leadership.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יתרו was a foreign priest, as far from the Jewish people as you can get. One invitation to a meal earned his family seats in the לשכת הגזית, where the סנהדרין sat. The next step brings the פסוקים that prove his descendants really sat there.

keyTerms.meaning: משה's father-in-law, a priest of מדין
The Chamber of Hewn Stone, where the סנהדרין sat

phrases.english: And it draws near the distant –
from Yitro,
as Rabbi Yochanan says:
In reward for 'Call him, that he may eat bread,'
phrases.notes: שמות 2:20. יתרו tells his daughters to invite משה in for a meal.

phrases.english: his grandchildren merited
and sat in the Chamber of Hewn Stone,

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמְקָרֶבֶת אֶת הָרְחוֹקִים מִיִּתְרוֹ דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the second power in the list, the opposite of the first: bringing outsiders close instead of pushing relatives away.
steps.raayaObject: That giving food 'draws near the distant.'
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's teaching that יתרו's descendants sat in the לשכת הגזית as a reward for his invitation.

steps.title: Proving from the פסוקים that יתרו's descendants were scribes
steps.stepSummary: Two פסוקים are joined. One says the families of scribes were the קינים, and the other says the קינים were the family of משה's father-in-law.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'And the families of scribes who dwelt in Jabez; the Tirathites, the Shimeathites, the Sucathites. These are the Kenites who came from Hammath, father of the house of Rechab.' And it is written there: 'And the children of the Kenite, משה's father-in-law, went up from the city of palm trees with the children of יהודה to the wilderness of יהודה, south of Arad; and he went and dwelt with the people.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רבי יוחנן's claim with two פסוקים. Joining them shows that the scribes were יתרו's descendants.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק says the families of scribes were the קינים. The second פסוק says the קינים were the children of 'the Kenite, משה's father-in-law,' meaning יתרו. Put together, יתרו's descendants were Torah scribes, the people who sat with the סנהדרין.

keyTerms.meaning: The Kenites, the family of יתרו
And it is written there (bringing a second פסוק to connect)

phrases.english: As it is stated: 'And the families of scribes who dwelt in Jabez;
phrases.notes: דברי הימים א 2:55

phrases.english: the Tirathites, the Shimeathites, the Sucathites.
These are the Kenites who came
from Hammath, father of the house of Rechab,'
and it is written there:
'And the children of the Kenite, Moses' father-in-law,
phrases.notes: שופטים 1:16. This is the link: the קינים are יתרו's family.

phrases.english: went up from the city of palm trees
with the children of Judah to the wilderness of Judah
which is in the south of Arad;
and he went and dwelt with the people.'

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר וּמִשְׁפְּחוֹת סוֹפְרִים יֹשְׁבֵי יַעְבֵּץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source in the פסוקים for רבי יוחנן's claim in step 2.
steps.raayaObject: That יתרו's descendants became scribes sitting in the לשכת הגזית.
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברי הימים א 2:55 (the scribes were קינים) together with שופטים 1:16 (the קינים were משה's father-in-law's family).

steps.title: Hospitality makes Heaven look away from the wicked: the source is מיכה
steps.stepSummary: The third power, that לגימה 'averts eyes from the wicked,' is proven from מיכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it averts eyes from the wicked: we learn this from מיכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the third example. מיכה, an idol worshipper, was not punished right away because he fed others.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מיכה set up an idol, which should have brought quick punishment. Because he kept his bread available to travelers, Heaven 'looked away' from his sin. Hospitality protected even a wicked person.

keyTerms.meaning: Makes eyes look away (Heaven overlooks sins)
The man who set up an idol in the days of the judges (שופטים 17)

phrases.english: And it averts eyes from the wicked –
from Micah.
phrases.notes: This points back to מיכה's idol, discussed just before: he was spared because his bread was open to travelers.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַעֲלֶמֶת עֵינַיִם מִן הָרְשָׁעִים מִמִּיכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the third power in רבי יוחנן's list.
steps.raayaObject: That giving food 'averts eyes from the wicked.'
steps.raayaSupportSource: The case of מיכה, who was not punished for his idol because he fed travelers.

steps.title: Hospitality brings the שכינה even onto a false prophet
steps.stepSummary: The fourth power, that לגימה 'causes the שכינה to rest on the prophets of בעל,' is proven from the colleague of עדו הנביא, who received real prophecy while hosting עדו.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it causes the שכינה to rest on the prophets of בעל: we learn this from the colleague of עדו הנביא, as it is written: 'And it was as they sat at the table, that the word of God came to the prophet who had brought him back.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the fourth example. A false prophet hosted עדו for a meal, and right there at the table God's word came to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The old prophet who brought עדו back to eat was a false prophet. Yet the פסוק says that while they sat at the table, God's word came to him. Hosting a guest was so great that it brought real prophecy to someone who did not deserve it.

keyTerms.meaning: Causes the Divine Presence to rest (brings prophecy)
Prophets of בעל, meaning false prophets
The prophet sent to warn ירבעם (מלכים א 13)

phrases.english: And it causes the Divine Presence to rest on the prophets of Baal –
from the colleague of Iddo the prophet,
as it is written: 'And it was as they sat at the table,
phrases.notes: מלכים א 13:20

phrases.english: that the word of God came to the prophet
who had brought him back.'
phrases.notes: This is the false prophet who talked עדו into coming back to eat with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַשְׁרָה שְׁכִינָה עַל נְבִיאֵי הַבַּעַל מֵחֲבֵירוֹ שֶׁל עִדּוֹ הַנָּבִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the fourth power in the list; the fifth follows in the next step.
steps.raayaObject: That giving food 'causes the שכינה to rest on the prophets of בעל.'
steps.raayaSupportSource: מלכים א 13:20: God's word came to the false prophet while he sat at the table hosting עדו.

steps.title: The fifth power: a careless mistake about food counts as deliberate
steps.stepSummary: The fifth power of לגימה, that a mistake involving it counts as if done on purpose, is proven from יהונתן, who did not give דוד bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a mistake involving it counts as if done on purpose. As רב יהודה said in the name of רב: If יהונתן had lent דוד two loaves of bread, the city of נוב, the city of the כהנים, would not have been killed, דואג האדומי would not have been driven out, and שאול and his three sons would not have been killed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the last power of לגימה from the list: a careless mistake about food is treated like a deliberate act. It proves this from what happened when יהונתן did not give דוד food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יהונתן did nothing wrong on purpose; he simply did not give דוד bread when he fled. Because of that small slip, דוד had to ask the כהנים of נוב for food, and a long chain of disasters followed. A small mistake about food was punished as harshly as a deliberate sin.

keyTerms.meaning: If only; had it been that
Was driven out (here, from עולם הבא)

steps.whatToRemember: All five powers of לגימה are now proven: it pushes away the close, brings near the distant, makes Heaven overlook the wicked, brings the שכינה onto false prophets, and turns a mistake into a deliberate act.

phrases.english: And a mistake regarding it counts as deliberate,
phrases.notes: 'It' means לגימה. This is the fifth and last power on the list.

phrases.english: as Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav:
Had Jonathan lent David
two loaves of bread,
Nov, the city of the priests, would not have been killed,
and Doeg the Edomite would not have been driven out,
and Saul and his three sons would not have been killed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְשִׁגְגָתָהּ עוֹלָה זָדוֹן, דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of the powers of לגימה with the fifth and final one.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that a mistake involving לגימה counts as deliberate
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's statement about יהונתן not giving דוד bread and the disasters that followed

steps.title: Why is אחז not listed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה left out the wicked king אחז.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why did they not list אחז?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic: why the משנה does not list אחז among the kings with no share in עולם הבא. This question sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה names only ירבעם, אחאב and מנשה. אחז was also very wicked, so it is surprising that he is missing.

phrases.aramaic: וּמִפְּנֵי מָה לֹא מָנוּ אֶת אָחָז?
phrases.english: And for what reason did they not list Ahaz?
phrases.notes: 'They' means the תנאים of the משנה, who listed the kings with no share in עולם הבא.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִפְּנֵי מָה לֹא מָנוּ אֶת אָחָז
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the section on לגימה ends.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why אחז is missing from the משנה's list of wicked kings

steps.title: אחז sits between two righteous kings
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה בר אבא answers that אחז is placed between his righteous father יותם and his righteous son חזקיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה בר אבא said: Because he is placed between two righteous people, between יותם and חזקיהו.
steps.whatsHappening: The first answer: אחז is protected because his father and his son were both righteous.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being surrounded by a righteous father and a righteous son saves אחז from being listed.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba said:
Because he is placed between two righteous people,
between Jotham and Hezekiah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁמּוּטָל בֵּין שְׁנֵי צַדִּיקִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about אחז.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אחז is protected by his righteous father and righteous son.

steps.title: אחז felt ashamed before ישעיהו
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף gives a different answer: אחז felt shame in front of the נביא ישעיהו, as hinted in a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Because he felt shame before ישעיהו, as it says: 'And ה׳ said to ישעיהו: Go out now to meet אחז, you and שאר ישוב your son, at the end of the channel of the upper pool, on the road of the launderer's field.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives a second reason: אחז still felt ashamed in front of the נביא. He brings a פסוק as a hint.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Feeling shame shows that אחז still had some respect for the נביא, and that counts in his favor. The proof rests on the word 'כובס' in the פסוק, which the גמרא explains next.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהָיָה לוֹ בּשֶׁת פָּנִים מִישַׁעְיָהוּ,
phrases.english: Because he felt shame before Isaiah,
as it is stated: 'And the Lord said to Isaiah:
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 7:3

phrases.english: Go out now to meet Ahaz,
you and Shear-Jashub your son,
at the end of the channel of the upper pool,
on the road of the launderer's field.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהָיָה לוֹ בּשֶׁת פָּנִים מִישַׁעְיָהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to the same question about אחז.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אחז felt shame before ישעיהו, and that counts in his favor.

steps.title: What does 'כובס' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains how the word 'כובס' shows that אחז was ashamed, and gives two versions.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'כובס' mean? Some say: he covered his face and passed by. And some say: he put a launderer's basket over his head and passed by.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the word 'כובס' to show where אחז's shame appears in the פסוק. There are two opinions about what he did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion connects 'כובס' to 'כבש', meaning to hide: אחז hid his face. The second connects it to a launderer: he hid under a launderer's basket. Either way, he was trying to hide from the נביא.

phrases.english: What is 'koves'?
There are those who say:
that he covered his face and passed by,
phrases.notes: A play on words: 'כובס' sounds like 'כבש', to hide.

phrases.english: And there are those who say:
he turned a launderer's basket over his head and passed by.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי ״כּוֹבֵס״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the word in רב יוסף's פסוק that proves אחז was ashamed.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אחז hid his face, or hid under a launderer's basket, so that he would not face ישעיהו.

steps.title: Why is אמון not listed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the wicked king אמון is missing from the list.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why did they not list אמון?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same kind of question about another wicked king, אמון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אמון was also very wicked, so it is surprising that the משנה does not list him.

keyTerms.meaning: A wicked king of יהודה, the father of יאשיהו

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי מָה לֹא מָנוּ אֶת אָמוֹן?
phrases.english: For what reason did they not list Amon?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִפְּנֵי מָה לֹא מָנוּ אֶת אָמוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from אחז to another missing king.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why אמון is missing from the list

steps.title: Because of the honor of his son יאשיהו
steps.stepSummary: אמון is left out out of respect for his righteous son יאשיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because of the honor of יאשיהו.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer: listing אמון would shame his righteous son יאשיהו, so he is left out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A righteous son protects his father's honor. This answer leads straight into the next question.

phrases.english: Because of the honor of Josiah.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִפְּנֵי כְּבוֹדוֹ שֶׁל יֹאשִׁיָּהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about אמון.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The honor of his righteous son יאשיהו keeps אמון off the list.

steps.title: Then מנשה should be left out too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: מנשה had a righteous father, חזקיהו, so why is he listed?
steps.simpleTranslation: Then מנשה too should not be listed, because of the honor of חזקיהו!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back: if a righteous relative's honor protects a wicked king, מנשה should be protected by his righteous father חזקיהו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מנשה is listed in the משנה even though his father was righteous. That seems to contradict the reason just given for אמון.

keyTerms.meaning: A wicked king, the son of חזקיהו, who is listed in the משנה

phrases.english: Let Manasseh also not be listed
because of the honor of Hezekiah?

steps.triggerLanguage: מְנַשֶּׁה נָמֵי לָא נִמְנֵי מִפְּנֵי כְּבוֹדוֹ שֶׁל חִזְקִיָּהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason given for אמון.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that a righteous relative's honor keeps a wicked king off the list
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: מנשה had a righteous father, yet he is listed, so the honor of a relative does not seem to protect anyone.

steps.title: A son brings merit to his father, not the other way around
steps.stepSummary: A righteous son brings merit to his father, but a righteous father does not bring merit to his son, as shown by אברהם and ישמעאל and by יצחק and עשו.
steps.simpleTranslation: A son brings merit to his father, but a father does not bring merit to his son, as it is written: 'And no one saves from My hand.' אברהם does not save ישמעאל, and יצחק does not save עשו.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the protection works in only one direction: from son to father. This is why אמון is saved by his son, but מנשה is not saved by his father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A righteous son brings merit to the father who raised him. A righteous father cannot rescue a wicked son, and the פסוק plus the examples of ישמעאל and עשו prove this.

keyTerms.meaning: A son brings merit to his father

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule of 'a son brings merit to his father' is well known, and it shapes the rest of this section.

phrases.english: A son brings merit to the father,
a father does not bring merit to the son.
As it is written: 'And no one saves from My hand.'
phrases.notes: דברים 32:39

phrases.english: Abraham does not save Ishmael,
Isaac does not save Esau.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּרָא מְזַכֵּי אַבָּא, אַבָּא לָא מְזַכֵּי בְּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from מנשה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between a son protecting a father and a father protecting a son
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any righteous relative protects a wicked king.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a righteous son protects his father; a righteous father cannot save his wicked son.

steps.title: So אחז is left out because of his son חזקיהו
steps.stepSummary: Using the new rule, the גמרא says אחז is also left out because of the honor of his son חזקיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that you have reached this, אחז too was not listed because of the honor of חזקיהו.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to אחז and uses the new rule to give a simpler reason why he is not listed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבי ירמיה בר אבא said אחז is protected by both his father and his son. Now, based on the rule just learned, it is really his son חזקיהו who protects him.

keyTerms.meaning: Now that you have reached this point

steps.whatToRemember: אחז and אמון are both left off the list because of their righteous sons; מנשה is listed because a father's merit cannot save his son.

phrases.english: Now that you have arrived at this,
Ahaz too was not listed
because of the honor of Hezekiah.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא דְּאָתֵית לְהָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the new rule back to the earlier question about אחז.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: אחז is not listed because of the honor of his son חזקיהו.

steps.title: Why is יהויקים not listed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the wicked king יהויקים is missing from the list.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why did they not list יהויקים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about one more wicked king, יהויקים. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יהויקים was extremely wicked, so his absence from the list needs a reason.

keyTerms.meaning: A very wicked king of יהודה

phrases.aramaic: וּמִפְּנֵי מָה לֹא מָנוּ אֶת יְהוֹיָקִים?
phrases.english: And for what reason did they not list Jehoiakim?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִפְּנֵי מָה לֹא מָנוּ אֶת יְהוֹיָקִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to another missing king.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why יהויקים is missing from the list

steps.title: 'This and yet another' written on his skull
steps.stepSummary: The answer comes from רבי חייא בר רבי אבויה: the words 'this and yet another' were written on יהויקים's skull.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because of what רבי חייא בר רבי אבויה said: On the skull of יהויקים was written, 'This and yet another.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with רבי חייא בר רבי אבויה's report that 'this and yet another' was written on יהויקים's skull.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words mean he receives a double punishment, so he has already been punished in a special way. That is why the משנה does not need to list him.

phrases.english: Because of what Rabbi Ḥiyya son of Rabbi Avuya said,
as Rabbi Ḥiyya son of Rabbi Avuya said:
Written on the skull of Jehoiakim was
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording.

phrases.english: 'This and yet another.'
phrases.notes: This means he gets one punishment and then another on top of it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא בְּרַבִּי אֲבוּיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about יהויקים.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: יהויקים was marked for a special double punishment, shown by the words on his skull.

steps.title: The skull that would not stay buried
steps.stepSummary: רבי פרידא's grandfather found a skull with 'this and yet another' written on it at the gates of ירושלים, and it would not stay buried.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי פרידא's grandfather found a skull lying at the gates of ירושלים, and written on it was 'This and yet another.' He buried it, but it would not stay buried. He buried it again, but it would not stay buried.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that shows the skull and its writing. Each time the skull was buried, it came back up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The skull refusing to stay buried shows that even burial was denied to him. The story backs up רבי חייא בר רבי אבויה's report, and the next steps show what 'yet another' refers to.

phrases.english: Rabbi Perida's grandfather found a skull
that was lying thrown at the gates of Jerusalem,
and written on it was 'This and yet another.'
He buried it, but it did not stay buried,
he buried it, but it did not stay buried.

steps.triggerLanguage: זְקֵינוֹ דְּרַבִּי פְּרִידָא אַשְׁכַּח גּוּלְגֻּלְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tells the story behind the skull mentioned in the previous step.
steps.raayaObject: The writing 'this and yet another' on יהויקים's skull and his double punishment
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of רבי פרידא's grandfather finding the skull that would not stay buried

steps.title: The grandfather realizes the skull belongs to יהויקים
steps.stepSummary: רבי פרידא's grandfather understands that the skull that would not stay buried belongs to יהויקים, based on a פסוק in ירמיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: This is the skull of יהויקים, because the פסוק says about him that he will be buried like a donkey, dragged and thrown away.
steps.whatsHappening: The story from Step 18 continues. The grandfather links the strange skull to the פסוק that says יהויקים would have a 'donkey's burial'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A skull that keeps coming back up out of the ground fits the curse that יהויקים would never get a proper burial. So the writing on the skull and the פסוק together show whose skull this is.

keyTerms.meaning: A donkey's burial, meaning no real burial at all

phrases.english: He said: This is the skull of Jehoiakim,
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבי פרידא's grandfather from the last step.

phrases.english: as it is written about him:
"He shall be buried with the burial of a donkey,
dragged and thrown out, etc."
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 22:19

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר: גּוּלְגׇּלְתּוֹ שֶׁל יְהוֹיָקִים הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story from Step 18 by identifying the skull.

steps.title: The skull is honored, and then burned by mistake
steps.stepSummary: The grandfather wraps the skull in silk out of respect for a king. His wife thinks it belonged to his first wife and burns it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: He was a king, so I must not treat him with disrespect. He wrapped the skull in silk and put it in a box. His wife saw it and thought it was the skull of his first wife, which he could not forget. She lit the oven and burned it.
steps.whatsHappening: The story keeps going. The grandfather tries to honor the skull, but his wife misunderstands and burns it. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even a wicked king still gets some respect because he was a king. But the skull ends up burned anyway, which is an even worse disgrace than not being buried.

phrases.english: He said: He is a king,
and it is not right to treat him with disrespect.
He wrapped it in silk
and placed it in a box.
His wife saw it and thought:
This belonged to his first wife,
since he is not forgetting her.
phrases.notes: She thought he was keeping the skull because he still missed his first wife.

phrases.english: She lit the oven and burned it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר: מַלְכָּא הוּא, וְלָא אִיפְשָׁר לְזַלְזוֹלֵי בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story: what happened to the skull after it was identified.
steps.raayaObject: That יהויקים suffered a second disgrace
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of the skull being burned

steps.title: This explains 'this and yet another'
steps.stepSummary: The burning of the skull explains the words written on it: 'this and yet another'.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is what was written: 'This and yet another.'
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends by tying back to the writing on the skull. 'This' was the missing burial, and 'yet another' was the burning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17 said 'this and yet another' was written on יהויקים's skull, which is why he is not on the list of kings who lose עולם הבא. Now we see what it meant: he received two disgraces, and these took the place of the full punishment.
steps.whatToRemember: יהויקים is not on the list because his body was disgraced twice: no burial, and then his skull was burned.

phrases.english: That is what is written: "This and yet another."
phrases.notes: He means the words written on the skull, back in Step 17.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַיְינוּ דִּכְתִיב: ״זֹאת וְעוֹד אַחֶרֶת״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the meaning out of the story in Steps 18 to 20.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The two disgraces of יהויקים's body explain 'this and yet another' and why he is not listed.

steps.title: How חזקיהו's self-praise led to his children's exile
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר traces a chain: חזקיהו praised himself, then asked for a sign, then non-Jews ate at his table, and that caused exile for his children.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר taught: Because חזקיהו said 'I have done what is good in Your eyes,' he came to ask 'What is the sign?' Because he asked for a sign, non-Jews came and ate at his table. Because non-Jews ate at his table, he caused exile for his children.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new teaching about King חזקיהו. It shows how one small wrong step led to the next, ending in exile.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each step causes the next one: the self-praise leads to asking for a sign, and the sign (the sun moving backward) brought messengers from בבל to his table. Hosting them led to the exile of his children to בבל.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר:
phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:
Because of "And I have done what is good in Your eyes,"
phrases.notes: מלכים ב 20:3. These are חזקיהו's words when he prayed while sick.

phrases.english: came "What is the sign?"
phrases.notes: מלכים ב 20:8. He asked the נביא for a sign that he would be healed.

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁבִיל ״מָה אוֹת״ – גּוֹיִם אָכְלוּ עַל שׁוּלְחָנוֹ.
phrases.english: Because of "What is the sign?", non-Jews ate at his table.
Because non-Jews ate at his table,
he caused exile for his children.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from יהויקים to a new teaching about חזקיהו, who was mentioned in Step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חזקיהו's chain of actions, starting from self-praise, caused his children's exile.

steps.title: This supports the sage חזקיה's teaching about hosting non-Jews
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא supports the sage חזקיה, who taught that inviting and serving an idol worshipper at home causes exile for one's children, based on a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: This supports חזקיה, who said: Anyone who invites a non-Jew into his home and serves him causes exile for his children, as it says: 'And some of your sons, who will come from you, will be taken and will be servants in the palace of the king of בבל.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says the ברייתא backs up a teaching of the sage חזקיה. חזקיה's teaching is a general rule, and the story of King חזקיהו is an example of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חזקיה learns his rule from the פסוק spoken to King חזקיהו right after he hosted the Babylonian messengers. The ברייתא's chain (non-Jews ate at his table, so exile came) matches that rule exactly.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up חזקיה (a sage of the גמרא) with חזקיהו (the king). The names look alike, but they are two different people.

phrases.english: This supports Ḥizkiyya,
phrases.notes: This is the sage חזקיה, not King חזקיהו.

phrases.english: as Ḥizkiyya said:
Anyone who invites a non-Jew into his house
and serves him
causes exile for his children, as it is stated:
"And of your sons who shall come out from you,
[whom you shall father,] they shall take away,
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are added to make the quote of the פסוק complete.

phrases.english: and they shall be eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylonia."
phrases.notes: מלכים ב 20:18

steps.triggerLanguage: מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ לְחִזְקִיָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the ברייתא in Step 22 supports a teaching of the sage חזקיה.
steps.raayaObject: חזקיה's rule: hosting and serving an idol worshipper causes exile for one's children
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, and מלכים ב 20:18
steps.whyThisMatters: It turns the story of King חזקיהו into a general lesson about whom a person brings into his home.

steps.title: What did חזקיהו show the messengers?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוק about חזקיהו showing the Babylonian messengers his 'בית נכתה', and רב asks what that word means.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'חזקיהו was happy with them and showed them his בית נכתה: the silver, the gold, the spices, and the fine oil.' רב asked: What does 'בית נכתה' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק about the same visit of the Babylonian messengers and asks about one unclear word. This sets up three different answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'נכתה' is unusual, so it is not clear what חזקיהו actually showed them. The answers that follow each explain what he did wrong in a different way.

keyTerms.meaning: An unclear phrase, usually understood as 'his treasure house'

phrases.english: "And Hezekiah was happy with them,
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 39:2. 'Them' are the messengers from the king of בבל.

phrases.english: and showed them his beit nekhoto,
the silver and the gold

phrases.aramaic: וְאֶת הַבְּשָׂמִים וְאֵת הַשֶּׁמֶן הַטּוֹב וְגוֹ׳״.
phrases.english: and the spices and the fine oil, etc."
Rav says: What is "beit nekhoto"?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: מַאי ״בֵּית נְכֹתֹה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Stays with the visit of the Babylonian messengers from Step 22 and asks about a word in the פסוק.

steps.title: רב: His wife served them drinks
steps.stepSummary: רב explains that 'בית נכתה' means חזקיהו's wife came out and poured drinks for the guests.
steps.simpleTranslation: His wife poured drinks for them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers his own question. He reads the phrase as being about חזקיהו's wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רב's reading, the 'house' is the wife, and חזקיהו showed off his family's private life by having her serve the foreign guests. This is a more personal kind of showing off than displaying money.

phrases.english: His wife poured drinks for them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִשְׁתּוֹ הִשְׁקְתָה עֲלֵיהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב's question from Step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'בית נכתה' means his wife served the guests drinks.

steps.title: שמואל and רבי יוחנן: His treasury, or a powerful weapon
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says חזקיהו showed them his real treasure house. רבי יוחנן says he showed them a weapon strong enough to destroy other weapons.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: He showed them his treasure house. רבי יוחנן said: He showed them a weapon that destroys other weapons.
steps.whatsHappening: Two more אמוראים give different answers to the same question about 'בית נכתה'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל reads the phrase simply, as the place where treasures are kept. רבי יוחנן says it was something even more dangerous to show foreigners: his strongest weapon. In all three answers, חזקיהו showed off something he should have kept private.
steps.whatToRemember: Three views of 'בית נכתה': רב says his wife, שמואל says his treasury, and רבי יוחנן says his strongest weapon.

phrases.english: And Shmuel says:
He showed them his treasure house.
And Rabbi Yoḥanan says:
He showed them a weapon that destroys weapons.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: בֵּית גְּנָזָיו הֶרְאָה לָהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives two other answers to the same question that רב answered in Step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שמואל: his treasure house. רבי יוחנן: a weapon that destroys other weapons.

steps.title: Why the destruction is mourned with the word 'איכה'
steps.stepSummary: רבא, in the name of רבי יוחנן, says the Jewish people were struck with 'איכה' because they broke the 36 sins in the Torah that carry the punishment of כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the פסוק 'How does the city sit alone,' רבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Why were the Jewish people struck with the word 'איכה'? Because they broke the thirty-six sins in the Torah that are punished with כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic: the exile and destruction, explained through the first word of מגילת איכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The letters of 'איכה' add up to 36. רבי יוחנן links that number to the 36 sins punished with כרת, showing that the lament matches exactly what the people did wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: How?, the word of mourning that opens מגילת איכה
A heavenly punishment of being cut off

phrases.english: "How does she sit alone"
phrases.notes: איכה 1:1

phrases.english: Rava says that Rabbi Yoḥanan says:
Why were the Jewish people struck with "eikha"?
Because they transgressed
the thirty-six sins punishable with karet in the Torah.
phrases.notes: The letters of איכה add up to 36: א is 1, י is 10, כ is 20, and ה is 5.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״אֵיכָה יָשְׁבָה בָּדָד״. אָמַר רָבָא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the exile of חזקיהו's children to the larger exile and destruction mourned in מגילת איכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The word 'איכה' (36) matches the 36 sins punished with כרת that the people broke.

steps.title: Why איכה is written in alphabetical order
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that the Jewish people were mourned with an alphabetical lament because they broke the תורה, which was given using the אלף בית.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Why were they struck with a lament arranged by the letters אלף בית? Because they broke the תורה, which was given using the אלף בית.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן adds a new teaching about the book of איכה, explaining why its chapters follow the order of the alphabet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The punishment matches the sin. The תורה was written with the letters of the אלף בית, so when Israel broke the תורה, their sorrow was also written letter by letter, from א to ת.

keyTerms.meaning: The Hebrew alphabet. Here it refers to the alphabetical order of איכה

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
Why were they struck with the alef-beit?
phrases.notes: Most chapters of איכה are written in alphabetical order, with each פסוק starting with the next letter.

phrases.english: Because they violated the Torah
which was given with the alef-beit.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִפְּנֵי מָה לָקוּ בְּאָלֶף בֵּית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of step 27 (Israel struck with 'איכה') by explaining the alphabetical structure of the book.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The alphabetical form of איכה is a measure-for-measure response to breaking the תורה, which was given in the letters of the אלף בית.

steps.title: 'Sitting alone': a blessing turned into a punishment
steps.stepSummary: רבא, quoting רבי יוחנן, says that הקדוש ברוך הוא promised Israel a safe and blessed solitude, but now their solitude will be lonely and sad.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'She sits alone.' רבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: הקדוש ברוך הוא said, 'I said, "Israel will dwell safely, alone, the fountain of יעקב, in a land of grain and wine, and its heavens will drip dew." Now their dwelling will be alone.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts explaining the first פסוק of איכה, phrase by phrase. Here it explains the words 'sits alone.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same word, בדד ('alone'), appears in a blessing in דברים. There it meant being separate in a good way: safe and rich. In איכה it turns into being alone in a painful way, abandoned and lonely.

phrases.english: "She sits alone."
phrases.notes: איכה 1:1

phrases.english: Rava said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
The Holy One, Blessed be He, said:
I said: "And Israel dwells in safety,
alone, the fountain of Jacob,
in a land of grain and wine;
also its heavens shall drip dew."
phrases.notes: דברים 33:28

phrases.english: Now their dwelling will be alone.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״יָשְׁבָה בָּדָד״. אָמַר רָבָא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the structure of איכה to explaining the words of its first פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'aloneness' in איכה is the painful reversal of the blessed, safe aloneness promised in דברים.

steps.title: 'The city full of people': marriages for many children
steps.stepSummary: רבא, quoting רבי יוחנן, explains that the city was full of people because they arranged marriages so that families would have many children.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'The city that was full of people.' רבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: They would marry a young girl to an older man and an older woman to a young man, so that they would have many children.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the next phrase of the פסוק, 'the city that was full of people,' and tells us how ירושלים became so crowded.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The city's large population did not happen by chance. People arranged matches across ages so that more couples could have children, which made the city very full. That makes the current emptiness even sadder.

phrases.english: "The city that was full of people":
Rava said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
That they would marry a young female to an older male
and an older female to a young male,
so that they would have many children.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״הָעִיר רַבָּתִי עָם״, אָמַר רָבָא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues to the next phrase of the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ירושלים was 'full of people' because marriages were arranged to produce many children.

steps.title: 'Like a widow': only a temporary separation
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה, quoting רב, says the word 'like' teaches that ירושלים is not truly widowed. She is like a wife whose husband went overseas and plans to come back.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'She became like a widow.' רב יהודה said in the name of רב: Like a widow, but not really a widow. Rather, she is like a woman whose husband went overseas and plans to return to her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the phrase 'like a widow' and finds a message of hope in the word 'like.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק does not say 'a widow.' It says 'like a widow.' A real widow's husband is gone forever. Here the 'husband' (הקדוש ברוך הוא) has only gone away for now and intends to come back to Israel.
steps.whatToRemember: Even in the saddest פסוק of איכה, the word 'like' (כ) carries hope: the separation between הקדוש ברוך הוא and Israel is not permanent.

phrases.english: "She became like a widow":
Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
Like a widow, but not an actual widow,
but rather like a woman whose husband went
to a country overseas
and he intends to return to her.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״הָיְתָה כְּאַלְמָנָה״ – אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues to the next phrase of the same פסוק, now quoting a different speaker (רב).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Like a widow' means a temporary separation: the husband intends to return.

steps.title: 'Princess among the provinces': Jews rise wherever they go
steps.stepSummary: רבא, quoting רבי יוחנן, explains that wherever the Jews are exiled, they become officers and leaders for their masters.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Great among the nations, princess among the provinces.' רבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Every place they go, they become officers for their masters.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the last part of the פסוק, showing that even in exile the Jews rise to important positions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though Israel is exiled and under foreign rulers, they do not become lowly. They become 'princes', meaning officials, serving the very masters who rule them. This sets up the story that follows.

phrases.english: "Great among the nations, princess among the provinces":
Rava said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
Every place that they go,
they become officers for their masters.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״רַבָּתִי בַגּוֹיִם שָׂרָתִי בַּמְּדִינוֹת״ – אָמַר רָבָא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes explaining the phrases of the first פסוק of איכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wherever Israel is exiled, they rise to become officials for their rulers.

steps.title: A ברייתא begins: two captives on הר הכרמל
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא opens a story about two Jewish people taken captive on הר הכרמל, with their captor walking behind them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: There was an incident with two people who were taken captive on הר הכרמל, and their captor was walking behind them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a story from a ברייתא. Here we only get the opening scene, and the story continues in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This step only sets the scene: two captives, a mountain, and a captor walking behind them. Coming right after the teaching that Jews become officers wherever they go, the story most likely shows Jewish wisdom even in captivity, but the details still have to unfold.

keyTerms.meaning: An incident, a story that happened

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
There was an incident with two people
who were taken captive on Mount Carmel,
and the captor was walking behind them.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מַעֲשֶׂה בִּשְׁנֵי בְּנֵי אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from explaining the פסוק to a story, apparently tied to the theme of step 32 (Jews rising in exile).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Opening scene of a story: two Jews taken captive on הר הכרמל, with their captor walking behind them.
